title: Licensing and Source Header Contract
readerIntent: Preserve the repository's canonical source header and avoid inconsistent generated or handwritten legal text.
owner: Repository license agreement and Nodics copyright-quality/generation contracts
summary: Every Nodics-owned handwritten, generated, template, and customer-skeleton JavaScript source uses the same tooling-owned 2026 header; documentation explains enforcement but does not grant or reinterpret legal rights.

sections.heading: Legal boundary
paragraphs: The applicable repository distribution and license agreement controls use, modification, and redistribution. This page is an engineering consistency contract, not legal advice and not an additional license grant. Ask the authorized Nodics legal or repository owner when rights or obligations are unclear.

sections.heading: Files covered
items: Nodics-owned handwritten JavaScript source.
Generated JavaScript source and regenerated artifacts.
JavaScript templates and module/project skeleton files.
Customer project JavaScript skeletons generated by Nodics tooling.
JavaScript snippets presented as complete Nodics source/template examples.

sections.heading: Rules
items: Use the canonical 2026 Nodics source header supplied and validated by repository tooling.
Do not hand-edit one file, module, provider, template, or generated artifact to use alternate copyright years, spelling, ownership, or legal wording.
When the canonical text changes, update the tooling copyright quality service, shared header utility, structure/module generators, templates, tests, documentation, and regenerated artifacts together.
Markdown pages do not require the JavaScript block header at the top; repository-owned metadata/data formats follow their governing file contract.
Third-party source, notices, generated vendor code, and dependencies retain their applicable upstream licenses and must not be relabeled as Nodics-owned code.
Do not remove attribution, notices, or license files without explicit legal/repository-owner approval.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Run `npm run quality:copyright` to detect missing, duplicated, malformed, or stale Nodics JavaScript headers.
Use `npm run quality:copyright:fix` only for the repository-governed normalization it supports, then review the complete diff.
Regenerate templates/artifacts through their owner rather than manually correcting every output.
Run structure, documentation, generated-context, focused, and regression gates affected by header/tooling changes.
A clean header check proves format consistency; it does not prove third-party license compatibility or resolve legal questions.

sections.heading: Contributor procedure
items: Before copying code, assets, documentation, models, examples, or generated output, identify its source, license, attribution, redistribution terms, modification requirements, and compatibility with the target repository.
Record decisions in the repository's approved legal and dependency process. Do not infer permission from public availability or remove notices merely to make generated files look consistent.
Provider SDKs, UI templates, fonts, icons, images, datasets, and model outputs may carry different obligations from application code and require separate review.
Escalate ambiguous ownership or commercial terms before implementation; technical convenience does not override legal authority.

sections.heading: Release and audit
items: Recheck dependency manifests, lock files, bundled assets, generated distributions, notices, source offers, and documentation links during release.
Ensure customer-project material is not accidentally incorporated into reusable framework packages and that framework licenses are preserved in downstream distributions.
Automation can inventory and flag changes, but an authorized reviewer decides policy and exceptions. Store the decision with version and evidence.
When a violation is found, contain distribution, preserve evidence, identify affected versions, replace or remove the material safely, update notices, and document remediation.

sections.heading: Complete guide: Licensing And Header Contract
paragraphs: This page defines the Nodics file-header and licensing rule for framework source, generated files, templates, examples, documentation, and customer project skeletons.

The rule is intentionally simple: the legal/header contract is part of the platform governance surface. Humans, AI tools, generators, and fix commands must apply the same standard instead of inventing file-by-file wording.

sections.heading: Standard Source Header
paragraphs: Every JavaScript file that is owned by Nodics framework source, generated by Nodics tooling, or created as a Nodics project/module/server/node skeleton must start with this header:

```javascript
/*
    Nodics - Enterprice Micro-Services Management Framework

    Copyright (c) 2026 Nodics All rights reserved.

    This software is the confidential and proprietary information of Nodics ("Confidential Information").
    You shall not disclose such Confidential Information and shall use it only in accordance with the
    terms of the license agreement you entered into with Nodics.

 */
```
Files with a Unix shebang, such as executable Node.js scripts, keep the shebang as the first line and place the standard header immediately after it.

sections.heading: Where The Header Is Required
paragraphs: The standard header is required for:
pipeline, interceptor, utility, data, and test JavaScript files;
schema, API, CRUD, test, and context surfaces;
files created by structure generation;
project modules.

Generated artifacts are not hand-maintained. The generator must emit the header from the canonical tooling contract, and `npm run quality:copyright:fix` may normalize generated output when the canonical text changes.

sections.heading: Documentation And Markdown
paragraphs: Markdown documentation does not need the JavaScript block header at the top of every file. Public documentation, README files, AGENTS files, and LLM contracts should explain behavior, ownership, extension paths, and governance rules without adding source-style boilerplate to every page.
When a documentation page shows a JavaScript skeleton or template, the snippet must use the current 2026 standard source header.

sections.heading: Third-Party And Excluded Files
paragraphs: Do not overwrite third-party compatibility code or vendor-owned files with the Nodics header unless Nodics owns the file. Exclusions must be explicit in the copyright quality service and documented by reason.
The current governance excludes `gFramework/nConfig/bin/enum.js` because it is a bundled third-party enum compatibility implementation.

sections.heading: Customer Project Skeletons
paragraphs: Generated customer project skeletons follow the same header unless a customer project has a legally approved replacement contract. A project-specific legal header must be implemented by replacing or extending the generator and copyright quality service through governed project tooling.
Do not change header text inside individual generated files after generation. Change the canonical generator/checker and regenerate or normalize the output.

sections.heading: Enforcement
paragraphs: Use:

```bash
npm run quality:copyright
npm run quality:copyright:fix
```

The enforced checker is owned by nTooling. It validates all JavaScript files that are in repository scope, skips private reference material under `docs/`, and preserves shebangs while normalizing the standard header.
Before committing a header or licensing change, run:

```bash
npm run quality:copyright
npm run test:tooling
npm run llm:validate
```
Run broader gates when the change also affects generators, generated artifacts, module structure, or release contracts.
